blocks.text: Most of Turkmenistan is desert. The Karakum, *Garagum* in Turkmen, covers about 70 percent of the country, some 350,000 square kilometres, and stretches about 800 km from west to east. Its name means **black sand**: *gara* (black) and *gum* (sand).

It is not one sea of bare dunes. Britannica divides it into a raised northern part, a low central part and a south-eastern part crossed by salt marshes. Crescent-shaped dunes, called barchans, cover less than a tenth of it, some of them over 9 metres high; elsewhere grasses and shrubs hold the sand in place. Rain is rare, roughly 70 to 150 mm a year, and summers are very hot.

The tree of the desert is the saxaul, *sazak* in Turkmen, a hardy shrub or small tree that grows in white and black kinds. In the south-east, the Repetek reserve was set up in the late 1920s to protect a typical piece of sandy desert with its woods of black saxaul, and UNESCO has listed it as a biosphere reserve since the late 1970s. Goitered gazelles and many birds live there.

People have always lived around the edges of the desert rather than inside it: in the oases at the foot of the Kopetdag mountains, where Ashgabat stands, along the Murgap and Tejen rivers at Mary and Tejen, and along the Amu Darya at Türkmenabat. In the sands themselves, herders moved their sheep and camels, *düýe*, from well to well, *guýy*.

Since the 1950s the Karakum Canal has carried water from the Amu Darya westward along the southern edge of the desert, which made more farming possible around Mary and Tejen. Deep in the desert, near the village of Derweze, a crater of burning natural gas draws visitors at night. Its Turkmen name is *Garagum ýalkymy*, the Shine of the Karakum. It is usually said to have been lit in 1971, after Soviet drilling, but local geologists have given other dates, and the records are unclear.

blocks.title: To and from the desert
blocks.text: With this unit's endings: *çöl* (desert) gives *çöle* (to the desert) and *çölden* (from the desert, across the desert). *Ýol çölden geçýär*: the road goes through the desert.
With the words of this unit, you can read this:

blocks.tk: Garagum uly çöl. Çölde gum köp, suw az. Biz Aşgabatdan Mara gidýäris. Ýol çölden geçýär. Ol ýerde düýeler bar.
blocks.en: The Karakum is a big desert. In the desert there is a lot of sand and little water. We are going from Ashgabat to Mary. The road goes through the desert. There are camels there.

questions.q: About how much of Turkmenistan does the Karakum cover?
In *Ýol çölden geçýär*, what does *çölden* mean?
questions.explain: With *geçmek*, the ablative says what you pass **through** or **across**.

sources.title: Karakum Desert
sources.note: Turkmen Garagum, “black sand”; about 350,000 km² and 800 km from west to east; the northern, central and south-eastern parts; barchans on less than 10 percent of the area, some 9 m high or more

sources.title: Karakum Desert
sources.note: About 70 percent of Turkmenistan; rainfall of 70 to 150 mm a year; the Karakum Canal from the Amu Darya, begun in 1954; the oases of Mary and Tejen

sources.title: Turkmenistan: Relief and oases
sources.note: Most of the land is desert with scattered oases: the Kopetdag foothills, the Murgap and Tejen valleys and the Amu Darya, with Türkmenabat as the centre of its oasis

sources.title: Repetek
sources.note: The reserve in the East Karakum, founded in 1927 on 34,600 hectares of sand desert, with black saxaul woods in its hollows; other sources give 1928 for its founding and 1978 or 1979 for the biosphere listing

sources.title: Repetek Biosphere State Reserve (tentative list)
sources.note: In the south-eastern Karakum near Repetek station; a UNESCO biosphere reserve since 1979; large black saxaul woods; goitered gazelle; an Important Bird Area

sources.title: Darvaza gas crater
sources.note: Turkmen name Garagum ýalkymy; the widely repeated date of 1971; local geologists' account of a collapse in the 1960s and a fire lit in the 1980s; missing records
